notes: This contract pins the official C++ timestamped Update Attribute Values and Reflect Attribute Values declarations used by Umbra's bounded non-regional timestamped attribute-update family. It also records the official Retract service because delivered passels and the restored live designator are checked at the post-delivery terminal boundary. Focused lifecycle evidence now includes an ordinary non-regional passel preserved across callback-gated Time Constrained disable/re-enable before the matching grant, and local-delete companions that suppress a queued reflection after one receiver forgets the object while allowing later rediscovery and delivery; the three-member form proves an independent survivor still receives the original callback before its grant. A mixed non-regional companion now sends one timestamped passel to an immediate/nonconstrained member and a constrained member, then retracts before the constrained grant so only the delivered copy receives Request Retraction. A voluntary-source-resignation companion now drains one accepted passel through two independent constrained recipient ledgers after Unconditionally Divest Attributes, preserving the original producer and callback metadata before each TAR/NMR grant. Focused untimed save/restore evidence reconstructs one ordinary queued passel for a single recipient and for two independent constrained recipients, proving separate Flush Queue reflection followed by Request Retraction. The object-instance and object-class Request Attribute Value Update response companions keep the timestamped service call in explicit provider callback code and verify a real requester reflection. A terminal-tombstone companion saves a pre-existing MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted classification and proves a discarded post-save designator is invalid after restore. The contract deliberately keeps time-management, order-type, and object-instance/object-class request/provide surfaces in their own contracts so each cross-service dependency remains auditable without treating this composite case as conformance evidence.
